newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 26.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Burma has suspended the dredging of the Moei River as the conflict over the borderline threatens to blow up into a military confrontation with both sides beefing up troops just across the disputed section of the river. Members of the Local Thai-Burmese Border Committee have called an urgent meeting to find a way to defuse the tension after the first round of talks held on Saturday collapsed. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Democrat Party has urged the authorities to charge suspected drug trafficker Li Yun-chung with bribery or make him take the witness stand before extraditing him to the United States. This would force him to reveal who he had bribed to grant him bail in February which allowed him to flee to Burma, deputy Democrat leader Suthas Ngernmuen says. (THE NATION)

- Residents of Ban Krua Muslim community have vowed to fight to the death the Expressway and Rapid Transit Authority's (ETA) attempt to cut an expressway link through their land. About 1,000 residents took the vow in the presence of ETA Governor Ruangrit Poonsawat who met their representatives yesterday to persuade them to move out and pave the way for the construction of a section of the second-stage expressway. (BANGKOK POST)

- In a move to balance its traditional emphasis on ties with Asia and the Pacific, particularly Southeast and East Asia, Thailand is pushing for the establishment of a new regional group with its neighbours to the west. The new group, tentatively called Bist-ec and modelled on the successful Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), is expected to be officially launched at a June 4-7 meeting at the Foreign Ministry in Bangkok. (BANGKOK POST)

- Finance Ministry officials are to try and convince Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan to take more aggressive fiscal measures to stimulate the economy and maintain a balanced budget. Earlier, they suggested the government tackle the economic crisis with a comprehensive package of fiscal policies, but the Cabinet later adopted only an increase in excise taxes on nine items. (THE NATION)

- Some outdated laws blocking foreign investment in Thailand will be amended, according to Prime Minister's Office Minister Veerakorn Kamprakob. Certain laws barred foreign investors from using local natural resources, such as wood, as raw materials in their production. The board's proposal that the laws be changed, or a royal decree be issued to promote foreign investment, has been submitted to Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh. (BANGKOK POST)
